response.sql:
WITH telescope_counts AS (
  SELECT
    observstation,
    COUNT(*) as telescope_count
  FROM telescopes
  GROUP BY observstation
),
total_telescopes AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) as total_count FROM telescopes
)
SELECT
  tc.observstation,
  tc.telescope_count,
  tc.telescope_count::NUMERIC / tt.total_count::NUMERIC as share
FROM telescope_counts tc
CROSS JOIN total_telescopes tt
ORDER BY share DESC
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: The query includes only observatory stations that have at least one telescope. Observatory stations in the observatories table with zero telescopes are excluded from the result. This is the most natural reading of 'for each observatory station, count its telescopes,' combined with returning the top 10 by share.

alternatives.interpretation: If 'for each observatory station' is meant to include all stations in the observatories table (even those with no telescopes), use a LEFT JOIN from observatories to telescopes. Stations with zero telescopes would have share = 0 and appear at the bottom of the sorted result.
alternatives.sql:
WITH telescope_counts AS (
  SELECT
    o.observstation,
    COUNT(t.telescregistry) as telescope_count
  FROM observatories o
  LEFT JOIN telescopes t ON o.observstation = t.observstation
  GROUP BY o.observstation
),
total_telescopes AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) as total_count FROM telescopes
)
SELECT
  tc.observstation,
  tc.telescope_count,
  tc.telescope_count::NUMERIC / tt.total_count::NUMERIC as share
FROM telescope_counts tc
CROSS JOIN total_telescopes tt
ORDER BY share DESC
LIMIT 10;
